Package frc.lib.NinjasLib.localization

Class RobotPose

java.lang.Object
frc.lib.NinjasLib.localization.RobotPose
public class RobotPose extends Object
The robot's single source of truth for "where am I on the field". This is a singleton facade (accessed via get()) that every subsystem and command should query instead of maintaining its own pose estimate. Internally it keeps two NinjasSwervePoseTrackers in lockstep: a vision-fused estimate (getRobotPose()) and an odometry-only estimate (getOdometryOnlyRobotPose()) that ignores vision entirely, and delegates per-camera trust and sanity checks to the injected VisionStrengthCalculator and VisionFiltersCalculator.

If no instance has been set with setInstance(frc.lib.NinjasLib.localization.RobotPose), get() returns a disabled placeholder whose queries return default/zero values and whose updates are no-ops, so callers never need to null-check it.

  • Constructor Details

    • RobotPose

      public RobotPose(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveDriveKinematics kinematics, VisionStrengthCalculator visionStrengthCalculator, VisionFiltersCalculator visionFiltersCalculator)
      Constructs an enabled RobotPose, creating its vision-fused and odometry-only swerve pose trackers. On a real robot the trackers are seeded from the current gyro yaw and module positions via Swerve.get(); in simulation they are seeded with a zeroed gyro and module set, since Swerve.get() isn't available yet at construction time. Pass the result to setInstance(frc.lib.NinjasLib.localization.RobotPose) to make it the active instance.
      Parameters:
      kinematics - The swerve drive kinematics used to calculate odometry.
      visionStrengthCalculator - Determines how much to trust each incoming vision measurement.
      visionFiltersCalculator - Determines whether an incoming vision measurement should be rejected outright before it reaches the pose trackers.

    • get

      public static RobotPose get()
      Returns the shared RobotPose instance that the rest of the robot code should query. If setInstance(frc.lib.NinjasLib.localization.RobotPose) has not been called yet, logs an important event and returns a disabled instance (all queries return default/zero values, all updates are no-ops) so callers can use it safely without a null check.
      Returns:
      The active RobotPose instance, or a disabled placeholder if none was set.

    • setInstance

      public static void setInstance(RobotPose instance)
      Installs the RobotPose instance returned by future calls to get(). Should be called once during robot initialization, before any subsystem queries the robot's pose.
      Parameters:
      instance - The instance to install as the singleton.

    • setRobotPose

      public void setRobotPose(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d pose)
      Resets both the vision-fused and odometry-only pose estimates to the given pose (e.g. when placing the robot at a known starting position, or applying a full pose correction). On a real robot this keeps the current gyro yaw; in simulation, module positions are reset to zero.
      Parameters:
      pose - The pose to set the robot pose to.

    • resetGyro

      public void resetGyro(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d yaw)
      Re-zeros the physical gyro to the given yaw and immediately re-anchors the vision-fused pose estimate's rotation to match, so the reported heading doesn't jump on the next odometry update. Does not touch the odometry-only estimate.
      Parameters:
      yaw - The yaw to reset the gyro to.

    • addOdometryUpdate

      public void addOdometryUpdate(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModulePosition[] modulePositions, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d gyroYaw)
      Feeds a new wheel/gyro sample into both pose trackers, using the current time as the sample's timestamp. This is the main per-loop entry point for keeping the robot's pose current â€” call it once per periodic cycle with the latest module and gyro readings. Use addTimedOdometryUpdate(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModulePosition[], edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d, double) instead when replaying higher-frequency samples (e.g. from OdometryThread) that carry their own timestamps.
      Parameters:
      modulePositions - The current position of the swerve modules.
      gyroYaw - The current gyro yaw.

    • addTimedOdometryUpdate

      public void addTimedOdometryUpdate(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModulePosition[] modulePositions, edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d gyroYaw, double timestamp)
      Same as addOdometryUpdate(edu.wpi.first.math.kinematics.SwerveModulePosition[], edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Rotation2d), but with an explicit sample timestamp. Use this when replaying a backlog of samples captured at a higher frequency than the main loop (e.g. from OdometryThread's queues), so each sample is correctly ordered relative to buffered vision corrections instead of all being stamped with the current time.
      Parameters:
      modulePositions - The current position of the swerve modules.
      gyroYaw - The gyro yaw at the time of this sample.
      timestamp - The timestamp of this sample, in seconds (FPGA time).

    • addManualVisionUpdate

      public void addManualVisionUpdate(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d estimation, double timestamp, edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3,edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1> visionStrength)
      Applies a vision measurement directly to the vision-fused pose tracker, bypassing the configured VisionFiltersCalculator and VisionStrengthCalculator. Prefer addVisionUpdate(VisionOutput, double) for normal camera pipelines; use this when the caller has already decided the measurement is valid and how much to trust it.
      Parameters:
      estimation - The vision-measured robot pose.
      timestamp - The timestamp of the measurement, in seconds (FPGA time).
      visionStrength - Per-axis trust to apply to this measurement (x, y, theta); see NinjasPoseTracker.setVisionMeasurementStrength(edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3, edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1>).

    • addVisionUpdate

      public void addVisionUpdate(VisionOutput estimation, double timestamp)
      The standard entry point for feeding a camera pipeline's output into the robot's pose estimate. This is what vision subsystems should call once per camera result; it is the piece that decides whether a vision measurement is trustworthy and, if so, how much.

      Does nothing if the estimation reports no targets. Otherwise, runs the configured VisionFiltersCalculator to sanity-check the measurement (e.g. reject implausible poses) and the configured VisionStrengthCalculator to compute per-axis trust (e.g. weighted by distance to target and current odometry drift); only measurements that pass the filter are applied, via addManualVisionUpdate(edu.wpi.first.math.geometry.Pose2d, double, edu.wpi.first.math.Matrix<edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N3, edu.wpi.first.math.numbers.N1>). Whether the measurement passed and its computed strength are always logged, even when rejected.

      Parameters:
      estimation - One camera's vision pose estimate for this cycle.
      timestamp - The timestamp of the measurement, in seconds (FPGA time).
